I help executive leaders solve the challenges that keep them up at night—from compliance and data security to the high-stakes transition to cloud services and the imperative to modernize and transform.

My value is in delivering scalable, disruptive solutions that directly monetize AI and data, resulting in:

* Exponential Growth: Increasing sales and improving customer retention through advanced analytics.
* Operational Efficiency: Drastically cutting costs and mitigating risk across finance, risk, data, and customer experience.
* Systemic Modernization: Executing successful digitization and cloud conversion projects that are replicable and scalable across the entire business.

My lifelong passion for the banking industry—from product dynamics to market forces—is what fuels my curiosity and drives my commitment to innovation. Let's discuss how we can blend this experience with the enormous potential of AI monetization to achieve your next strategic goal.

Connect with me to explore what we can achieve together.

experience.position: Senior Managing Consultant, Financial Services (Big Data Analytics and Optimization)
experience.description:
OPPORTUNITY: Recruited to lead large-scale transformation programs, I quickly jumped into major projects that called for every one of the skills and strengths I had developed in prior roles.

Our clients—major US and global financial institutions—faced serious challenges and immediate threats to continued successful operation. Some needed to revise technologies, practices, and protections to comply with regulations around data privacy and money laundering. Others faced mandates from federal regulators and needed to make changes quickly. Some were being more proactive, looking to strengthen their operations to meet emerging business needs.

The largest challenge I faced in this role was helping a client meet a tight timeline for compliance with new Federal Reserve regulations. Nearly half of the allowed time period had passed, no progress had been made, and the prior consulting firm was ousted. I had to make the client believe we could do the job (spent 3 months in program planning and client presentations), then execute the job in only 6 months.

We hit a home run—becoming the only one of the 5 largest US banks to meet the deadline with a successful submission. The success of this project led to formalizing the methodology that has subsequently become the centerpiece of a new practice specialty at IBM.

ACHIEVEMENT HIGHLIGHTS:
►Successful CCAR submission, on time, completed in half the time other (unsuccessful) companies had
►Dominant position for IBM Global Business Services in the risk domain
►Reputation as a thought leader and numerous speaking engagements on issues related to emerging technologies for the banking industry

OPPORTUNITY: In my first consulting role, I had the great good fortune to work with institutions that had some of the largest and most complex data needs and challenges in the country—federal and city governments that required exceptional transparency, security, and data management.

In addition to managing large, complex programs, I gained skill and experience in managing client expectations and relationships, uncovering needs (spoken and unspoken), and matching solutions to sometimes limited budgets.

ACHIEVEMENT HIGHLIGHTS:
►Collaborating with the Federal CIO to introduce Open Source technology into the federal government.
►Managing an $85M contract for the White House (White House Transparency Initiative).
►Delivering 20+ projects annually and generating more than $20M revenue annually.

OPPORTUNITY: Two large, multi-year transformations provided a proving ground for my leadership skills and exposed me to the human elements of any major change, along with the technology aspects.

First, I led an Accounting and Finance transformation to restore the stability and accuracy of the reconciliation process. This was not a “nice to have” but rather a mandate from the SEC. Partnering with Deloitte, I developed a methodology that became the foundation for all future large programs. We implemented new technologies and processes that improved reporting, eliminated errors and discrepancies, streamlined regulatory reporting, and reduced our close period from 45 days to 6.

Next, we were challenged to implement President Obama’s new Making Home Affordable (MHA) program. This enormous initiative required us to transform all of our processes and move to a new technology platform. We ran 30+ large projects simultaneously.

ACHIEVEMENT HIGHLIGHTS:
►Complete modernization of Finance and Accounting; impeccable, on-time reporting.
►MHA program completion on time and with recognition for “flawless” execution.

headline:
Sustained Change through Customised Leadership Development: 
Author | Facilitator | Leadership Development | Consultant | Expert | Mentor | Coach
topSkills: Facilitation • Coaching • Instructional Design • Needs Analysis and Diagnostics  • Program Design
about:
I am a commercially astute and experienced professional with a passion for leadership development, executive education, and cultural transformation. With over 20 years of experience in diagnostics, design, and delivery of customised learning solutions, I’ve worked with leaders and organisations across the globe in industries such as banking, finance, healthcare, insurance, FMCG, pharmaceuticals, professional services, and telecommunications.

My focus is helping individuals and organisations unlock their potential and achieve sustainable growth. By blending evidence-based approaches and deep diagnostics with practical insights, I design and facilitate high-impact learning interventions that address complex challenges, build leadership capacity, and drive long-term, meaningful change.

Key Specialisations:
* Diagnostics and Needs Analysis – Identifying strategic learning needs and aligning them with organisational goals.
* Customised Programme Design and Delivery – Creating bespoke learning journeys and leadership academies that deliver measurable results.
* Facilitation, Coaching, and Mentoring – Partnering with leaders at all levels to foster growth, resilience, and agility.
* Cultural Transformation – Leading initiatives to embed core values, enhance collaboration, and build high-performance cultures.
I
’ve partnered closely with C-suite leaders and senior executives to develop leadership frameworks, succession planning strategies, and long-term programmes that achieve lasting impact. Collaboration and innovation are central to my approach, ensuring solutions are both strategic and practical.

As Managing Consultant at Intrepid Leadership Consulting, I support global organisations in building leadership capability and navigating change with agility and purpose. I’ve worked with leading companies such as Bupa Arabia, Deloitte, Deutsche Bank, KPMG, Novartis, Unilever, and Glencore, delivering transformational programmes aligned with their strategic goals.

In addition, I am the co-author of 50 Ideas That Changed the World of Work (Profile Books, 2025), which explores key trends shaping the workplace and offers insights into the evolving world of leadership.

I believe that collaboration is at the heart of our success and transformation, as well as the power of lifelong learning and the power of leadership & leadership development to transform organisations and lives. Whether designing diagnostic tools, facilitating development programmes, or mentoring emerging leaders, my focus is always on creating sustainable, lasting change.

publications.title: Joint, Interagency, and Tailored: Getting Security Force Assistance Right in Georgia
publications.description: This paper argues that security force assistance (SFA) is an important mission, and Georgia is an important partner within which to conduct that mission. But for it to be maximally effective, in Georgia or anywhere, it must account for things like absorptive capacity and institutional thresholds, and must take the form of a tailored approach that reflects those realities.

publications.title: The Military Moral Education Program
publications.description: This paper recommends changes that will require attention to the overarching education of the soldier as a moral agent. Moral education must educate soldiers so that they might discern right actions, and then choose to conduct those actions out of respect for the profession and its ethic. To develop a disposition of moral responsibility, we need to take a new approach to learning; we must encourage full-scale debates about moral issues (a dialectical method) that allows soldiers to question and deepen their personal convictions until they adopt the profession’s morals as their own. These changes to the military moral education program will benefit the military in two ways: collectively decreasing the occurrence of moral failures, and individually fostering greater resiliency against moral tragedy by appropriating soldiers’ morals within the greater Army ethic.

publications.title: Lessons from Yusufiyah: From Blackhearts to Changing Professional Military Education
publications.description: This article offers key lessons about how the Army can teach its soldiers the moral obligations they have to other human beings, and the choices for which soldiers must be accountable. It tells not only of Justin Watt’s, a soldier in the storied 101st Infantry Division,  moral courage and imagination but also of how he applied moral agency—making ethical decisions and taking ethical actions based on right and wrong.  Watt’s decision to report the crime would help wronged people whom he had never met obtain justice, and it would lead to four of his platoon members going to prison.

publications.title: "Walking the Last Mile Home" in the Strong Gray Line
publications.description:
This book is a collection of personal experiences from the West Point Class of 2004’s deployments and gives tribute to fallen comrades. The collective hope is that these stories help readers understand how over a decade of war changed some of its members; and, that the book provides some insights into the amazing classmates who paid the ultimate sacrifice for Country and Corps.  Pre-publication website at http://www.thestronggrayline.com/. 

Preview: 

"Keeping my word, I walked one more mile, then another, and another until we reached a pre-designated location on the river’s edge. My father had arranged for a canoe to taxi us across the Mekong River and, from there, we would make our journey to the refugee camps in Thailand. As we stepped into a small wooden boat, I gripped its sides and, not knowing how to swim, I sat in the middle of it and became fixated on the notion that at any moment our little vessel would capsize. I remember the cold water splashing onto my legs, quickly accumulating inside the boat’s bottom, and a sinking feeling swirled inside me. 

Baqubah, Diyala Province, Iraq. The same feeling swirled in my stomach after the Chinook, carrying my ten-man military training team, touched down on the pavement of Forward Operating Base (FOB) Gabe in Baqubah, Iraq. In the excitement of exiting the helicopter, my wedding ring slipped off my finger and rolled into the abyss. I frantically searched my pockets and every crease in my uniform and equipment to see if my precious ring would miraculously reappear, but no luck. It would never be seen again. Jenny was going to kill me, I thought. A month before, I had to say the usual tearful good-byes to her and our three-month-old son, leaving them in her hometown; and now, I would have to tell her that I had lost the very symbol of our commitment to one another. Although I knew she would eventually forgive me, I could not easily shake the feeling of unease as I began my second deployment to Iraq."

Contra Friedman: A Case for National Conscription
publications.publishedAt: Journal of Social Sciences and Humanities (JoSH), Issue 1, Winter 2016
publications.description: In this paper, I identify two popular cases for reinstituting the draft and use them to discuss some problems they pose for Friedman’s conception of an AVF. First, I present the issue of misrepresentation in the military force and explain how this is a threat to a healthy representative democracy. Further, I question if military members are merely means to accomplish an ill-defined end when their government sends them back repeatedly to fight wars. These soldiers return home and find that fellow citizens are happy to pat them on the back, praising them with words like “hero” and “patriot.” Yet, some of these same citizens have little understanding of the soldiers’ experiences or no interest in sharing the soldiers’ burden. This type of social apathy weakens civil society,  compartmentalizing people to their own private interests and increasing social and political risks, and will eventually require a form of conscription (as one measure amongst others) to correct this problem.

projects.title: Comparative Potencies of Native and Enriched Bovine and Porcine Heparins
projects.description:

headline: Executive Strategy Consultant - Higher Ed Transformation Leader - Former C-Suite University Executive - Deloitte Alum - Trusted Advisor - Equity-Driven Innovator
about:
With over two decades of C-suite leadership and four years advising top-tier universities and state agencies as an Executive Strategy Consultant, I specialize in guiding institutions through complex transformation. My work spans strategic planning, organizational redesign, student success innovation, and cross-divisional change management—grounded in data, driven by mission, and executed with precision.

I’ve led multimillion-dollar initiatives at Deloitte and served as a trusted advisor to presidents, trustees, and senior executives across five universities where (as a Vice President and Chief of Staff) I led divisions of 300 employees, 20 functional units, and budgets of over $100 million. Whether nurturing relationships with university leaders to build an $80M consulting pipeline, designing equity-centered retention strategies, creating new organization designs (and the change management model to support them), sponsoring risk management convenings, or co-leading Future of Work initiatives aligned with state workforce agencies and universities, I bring a rare blend of industry expertise, strategic insight, operational fluency, and inclusive thought leadership.

My expertise includes: developing and nurturing executive client relationships; communications and change management; organization re-design; strategic planning; shared services; risk, resilience and compliance; student success/lifecycle; equity gap elimination; career readiness and workforce development; student mental health; and athletics. 

I have utilized my strong interpersonal skills to build effective teams, and collaborate with many  University stakeholders. Institutional executives find me to be a valued thought partner, helping them think through how to address the numerous challenges facing their colleges and universities. 

I thrive in environments where collaboration meets complexity—where institutions seek not just improvement, but reinvention. My passion lies in helping higher education evolve to meet the demands of a changing world, while staying true to its core purpose: empowering human potential, just as my role models (my parents) did, as faculty members.

Open to opportunities, immersive travel, and thought leadership engagements that expand perspective and deepen impact.

receivedRecommendations.description: Dr. Eileen Sullivan is a skilled senior student affairs leader.  I witness her deep commitment to student success on a daily basis as she prioritizes student perspectives and needs in all of her decision making.  She has broad knowledge and skill in a variety functional areas and is adept at seeing how student affairs work fits into larger college/university priorities and plans.  In particular, I am inspired by the value she places on community and civic engagement as a way to help students shape their campus and communities in order to become global citizens post graduation.  She also demonstrates her willingness to lead from a place of cultural humility and centers the experiences of underrepresented and marginalized students, staff and faculty as she makes decisions.

receivedRecommendations.givenByHeadline: Vice President for Development at Garrett-Evangelical Theological Seminary
receivedRecommendations.givenAt: September 13, 2017, Joseph worked with Eileen on the same team
receivedRecommendations.description:
Eileen and I served together on the Elmhurst College president's cabinet for five years. She is a consummate students affairs professional. Eileen is particularly skilled and effective when helping students and their families work through challenges, particularly health or family emergency issues. Her experience as chief of staff to a public university president gives her a broad understanding of higher education administration and strategy beyond student affairs. 

Eileen is also well-versed in Title IX, the Cleary Act, and other college and university compliance issues. 

Our departments collaborated on student and alumni related events throughout each academic year. Eileen and her team were good partners and helped us create successful events at first-year student orientation, Homecoming, and Commencement.

receivedRecommendations.givenByHeadline: Associate Dean of Students, Elmhurst University
receivedRecommendations.givenAt: September 12, 2017, Michelle reported directly to Eileen
receivedRecommendations.description: Dr. Eileen Sullivan was an incredible supervisor, mentor and friend. She provided me multiple opportunities to grow as a Student Affairs professional. She constantly provided support, encouragement and growth. Eileen was not only the biggest advocate for her team but for the students. They referred to her as "Bean" and were constantly in her office to visit. She always had an open door, listening ear and safe space to go for the students. Her passion for the work she does is seen everyday in her actions. She knew how to push you for the better, was your biggest cheerleader and always knew how to make you laugh. She made the work environment enjoyable and a family. Dr.Eileen Sullivan would be an amazing asset to any institution and Student Affairs team. I value the time I worked for her and contribute my successes to her guidance and support.

receivedRecommendations.description: I'm really pleased to support Dr. Sullivan for positions in higher education.  In the time I worked with her, I was struck by her energy, her kindness, and her persistence in using research based practice to address chronic problems innovatively.  As a colleague, she kept  the interests of students first, but was interested in working collaboratively with stakeholders. I think of her as a person of high academic values, and great tenacity in doing what's right.

receivedRecommendations.givenByHeadline: Student Ombuds at Grand Valley State University
receivedRecommendations.givenAt: September 11, 2017, Takeelia reported directly to Eileen
receivedRecommendations.description: Dr. Sullivan was an amazing and dynamic supervisor. She was not afraid to try new things and the students loved her. Dr. Sullivan, Eileen, challenged and supported staff in a good way. She made sure that you were doing your job but also challenged you to do a bit more.  My time with Dr. Sullivan was great in the way that she supported and mentored you in your position. She never made anyone feel as if they didn't know what they were doing. She has always been a supportive and encouraging person. Students were her focus. Retention at the institution to help them graduate was huge on her list of things to do. Dr. Sullivan helped to create programs that focused on retention. She was also a big supporter of people within marginalized groups. This helped to encourage them to graduate and to know that they had an ally in her. She is an amazing teacher and leader!

receivedRecommendations.givenByHeadline: President at Roanoke College | Champion of Learner-Centered Innovation | Strategic Leader
receivedRecommendations.givenAt: September 8, 2017, Frank worked with Eileen but they were at different companies
receivedRecommendations.description: Eileen Sullivan is one of those rare individuals who possesses and uses the perfect combination of "head and heart" as a leader. She's smart, thoughtful, and equipped with loads of professional knowledge.  Yet Eileen is simultaneously kind, gracious, and endearing; people who work with her want to get things done. They are compelled and moved by Eileen's value-centric approach to leadership in higher education. As executive editor of About Campus, I had the privilege of working with Eileen as the author of a feature article, "Getting Schooled:  What one dean learned from one student with ASD." Read this article and you'll see what "heart" and "head" looks like in practice. It's an honor to call Eileen a colleague. She's a superstar in our profession.

receivedRecommendations.givenByHeadline: Full Time Mom / Mentor & Leadership Coach / Lifelong Learner
receivedRecommendations.givenAt: August 30, 2017, Katie worked with Eileen but on different teams
receivedRecommendations.description: I have personally and professionally known Eileen Sullivan for six years, with four of those years being an undergraduate student at Elmhurst College where Eileen served as the Senior Student Affairs Officer in the division of Student Affairs. As a highly involved undergraduate student leader, I worked closely with Eileen in a capacity of ways. Working in the Student Activities office provided space for me to connect with Eileen on a personal and professional level. As an Orientation Student Leader, Fraternity and Sorority Life Student Activities Assistant, Union Board (programming board) Executive Member and student who was highly interested in Student Affairs as a future profession, Eileen always made an effort to connect me with other offices, colleagues and professionals on Elmhurst’s campus.  The effort she placed in caring deeply for students was consistent and relevant in everything she did — including my own life.  Eileen models what it means to care deeply for students. I am thankful for the support Eileen offered me for those four years while at Elmhurst, and beyond.

receivedRecommendations.givenByHeadline: Higher Education Executive
receivedRecommendations.givenAt: August 25, 2017, Damon worked with Eileen but they were at different companies
receivedRecommendations.description:
Put simply, Eileen is a phenomenal student affairs leader. She and I frequently communicated while she was Dean of Students at Elmhurst. Each month during the academic year, all the senior student affairs administrators from the private schools of the West Suburban Chicago area would gather for lunch and discuss a number of salient topics in order to assist and support each other. 

Eileen was immediately a thought leader within the group and contributed an incredible amount of knowledge to her colleagues. It was clear that she was not only current on the latest trends in higher ed and the latest regulations, she had already started implementing changes at Elmhurst in response to these trends. She served as a model for the group, and many of the programs and services the rest of us implemented were as a direct result of first getting direction from Eileen. 

I value Eileen as a colleague and friend. Over the years, we've all grown to know each other well, and Eileen would always seem to remember something happening in my personal life about which she would ask at our monthly luncheons. She takes the time to listen and cares a great deal about other people. She's top notch in my book!

receivedRecommendations.givenAt: August 23, 2017, Frank worked with Eileen but they were at different companies
receivedRecommendations.description:
It is with great pleasure that I am writing a note of endorsement for Dr. Eileen Sullivan.  As the Provost at the University of St. Francis, I was aware of Eileen’s reputation as a great VP for Student Affairs at Elmhurst through my VP for Student Affairs who often referred to her as his mentor and model.  I also knew from Elmhurst’s CAO, Dr. Alzada Tipton, that Eileen worked very closely with her to grow and maintain a solid partnership between academic and student affairs.

My wife and I are also able to make an even stronger endorsement for Eileen as a Senior Student Affairs Officer (VP for Student Affairs/Dean of Students) from our perspective as parents.  We tragically lost our 19 year old son while he was a sophomore at Elmhurst College in 2010. Not only were my wife and I devastated, but my son’s friends were shocked and distraught. Eileen immediately and effectively used University and personal resources to provide counseling, comfort and spiritual support to both the students and my wife and I.  She facilitated meetings, concerts, services, and anything that the students and parents needed.  While losing our son was a tragedy, Eileen’s efforts allowed my wife and me to join my son’s friends in finding ways to cope and share our grief. 

I cannot be stronger in my recommendation of Eileen for a Senior Student Affairs Officer.  Her combination of humanity and administrative skills makes her the perfect person to both work with students/parents and to serve in a chief administrative role.

receivedRecommendations.givenByHeadline: First generation college graduate committed to creating access and opportunity for others
receivedRecommendations.givenAt: August 22, 2017, Rich worked with Eileen but they were at different companies
receivedRecommendations.description: I’ve had the pleasure of knowing Eileen for the better part of three decades.   We first met when I was a graduate student at Eastern Illinois University.  Our professional journeys were inter-twined for many years.   The first significant and substantive connection was forged as Chief Student Affairs officers supervising Division III athletics programs.  I developed a greater appreciation for Eileen’s depth and understanding of higher education when we were in residence at one of the institutes offered by the Graduate School of Education at Harvard.  I have followed her career and consider her a touch point in the ever changing world of higher education.  If the opportunity presented itself, I would welcome her to my team without reservation.

receivedRecommendations.givenByHeadline: Vocational Coach at Ambitions Community Support Services of Washington
receivedRecommendations.givenAt: August 21, 2017, Eileen was senior to Meredithe but didn't manage Meredithe directly
receivedRecommendations.description: I knew Dr. Sullivan as the Dean of Students at Elmhurst College, during my time as a student (2011-2015).  As a student leader, Dr. Sullivan provided endless support to not only me but to the entire student body.  Dr. Sullivan went above and beyond in her unconditional support of students with developmental disabilities by ensuring they got the support they needed both in and out of the classroom.   My senior year, I served as the President of the Student Government Association.  As my adviser, Dr. Sullivan encouraged me to fight for important issues such as putting gender neutral restrooms in the student union.   Dr. Sullivan has been instrumental in my growth both personally and professional and has served as a mentor as I have entered the field of Student Affairs and Higher Education.

receivedRecommendations.givenByHeadline: Vice President for Academic Success and Student Affairs & Dean of Students at Kansas State University
receivedRecommendations.givenAt: August 21, 2017, Thomas worked with Eileen on the same team
receivedRecommendations.description: I had the opportunity to work with Eileen in developing the Senior Student Affairs Office Institute at the 2017 joint NASPA IV W/E conference held in St. Louis, MO. Eileen was a joy to work with and I had the opportunity to witness first-hand her commitment to the student affairs profession throughout our planning. She is a highly effective presenter and approaches her work with strong detail-orientation and commitment.  It was evident in our planning that Eileen has a deep understanding of the complex issues facing student affairs leaders and is effectively strategic in her approach in tackling such issues, especially those centered around meeting student needs. I greatly appreciated the opportunity I had to develop a program with her and would highly and unreservedly recommend her for a student affairs leadership position.

receivedRecommendations.givenByHeadline: Senior Associate Vice President, Enrollment Management Solutions
receivedRecommendations.givenAt: August 21, 2017, Art worked with Eileen but on different teams
receivedRecommendations.description: I have had the pleasure of knowing Eileen Sullivan for more 10 years and she is a superb Student Affairs practitioner and leader within higher education, an ardent advocate for students, and a competent administrator.  I have interacted with her within her professional capacity, most notably when she served as Dean of Students at Elmhurst College, and through our national organization, NASPA.  She continually impressed me as a supportive, intelligent, empathetic, and reasoned higher education administrator.  She is someone that I readily turn to for counsel and trust in the advice she imparts.  I would, without reservation, recommend Eileen Sullivan as a higher education administrator and leader that we would all do well to emulate.

receivedRecommendations.givenByHeadline: Vice President for Mission Integration
receivedRecommendations.givenAt: August 17, 2017, Donald "DJ" worked with Eileen on the same team
receivedRecommendations.description: During my time as assistant professor and program coordinator for the M.Ed. in Higher Education program at Grand Valley State University, I had the privilege of working closely with Dr. Sullivan who oversees the graduate assistant placement and professional development process for students in our M.Ed. program. I quickly learned she is a change agent, compassionate to students need, embraces the values of diversity, equity and inclusion, and often “gets it right.” In addition, it was refreshing that she understands faculty and our roles in universities settings, which I attribute to her academic background in higher education and her experience as an adjunct professor and graduate capstone advisor (i.e., theses, dissertations).  In short, I can’t say enough good about “Dean Bean” and thoroughly enjoyed working with her as a colleague. Any institution would benefit from her talents, and I'm glad I benefited from her talents as a colleague.

slides.title: Increasing Value and Productivity through Modern Legal Service Delivery Models
slides.subtitle: Robert Taylor on LinkedIn
slides.description: The sea change in the legal industry that has been foreshadowed for well over a decade may finally be underway showing that leading legal departments are seeking better, faster, and value driven service delivery. While most legal work is still done in traditional models and under traditional hourly business agreements, a recent survey indicates real momentum for new approaches. According to the 15th Annual Blickstein Group Law Department Operations Survey, done in collaboration with Deloitte, more than 30% of law departments expect their spending with alternative legal service providers (ALSPs) to increase in the next 12 months, and none expect their spending to decrease. It’s becoming clear that more in-house legal departments are deploying ALSPs (as just one example of new legal service delivery models), and there is seemingly more openness to adopting alternative sourcing than perhaps ever before. Additionally, leading practices among legal departments recognize that not all legal services are homogenous in terms of business value created, contribution to strategic goals, complexity and risk profile. They also recognize that Legal departments in the future must make deliberate resourcing decisions on what work is best performed where, how, and by whom. This entails a clear-eyed assessment of business priorities, availability of investment, cultural preferences and changing needs for capital costs vs. operating costs. One perspective on legal work is categorizing it into three general buckets: Cream, Core, and Commodity. A “bet the company” piece of litigation might be classified as “cream,” meaning it is worthwhile and necessary to engage bespoke services from top attorneys at leading law firms to mitigate unacceptable risk or take full advantage of a complex opportunity. Other legal work, including third-party subpoenas or e-discovery document reviews, may be seen as a “commodity” because it can be done in largely the same way every time with less expensive resources with reduced risk. Often overlooked, however, is a third, and likely the largest, bucket, which is every day – or “core” – legal work. We define core legal work as the bread-and-butter matters that in-house counsel and their law firms do that keeps the company running on an ongoing basis. It may occasionally vary or escalate but is mostly predictable and repeatable. It is not sensible business practice to charge for – or pay for – all legal work as if it is bet-the-company litigation. That may make the “core” work ripe for disruption. As the legal ecosystem becomes more diverse and better funded, alternatives to the traditional methods of providing legal services – namely, tailored service by hourly billers at law firms – have become more prevalent. Simply put, organizations are finding new ways to get legal work done. These alternative legal service delivery models include automation and self-service, flexible staffing, and offerings from ALSPs. The Difference Between Delivery Models and Billig Models Alternative legal service models are not the same as alternative billing models, also known as alternative fee arrangements or AFAs. While most alternative delivery models typically make sense with an AFA in place, “time-based” AFAs are sometimes applied to work done under traditional models. These time-based AFAs are predicated on the number of hours it takes a firm to do the work at a specified unit price. And while those hours are repackaged for the client into a different commercial model, the providers are still selling time. New legal service delivery models, however, may require services to be delivered using some novel combination of people, processes and technology, which can reduce the time spent on a matter. A value-based AFA, based not on inputs such as time but on outputs and results, may make more sense. When legal processes are delivered in new ways, it is often logical to bill them in new ways, too. Alternatives for Core Legal Work Most attorneys, of course, look at work through a legal lens. Different areas of work may not seem to have much in common from that perspective. Negotiating contracts and drafting pleadings, for example, may require completely different legal expertise. They may not even be in the same type of practice, as contracts are a commercial enterprise and pleadings are part of litigation. When looking at legal work through an engineering lens, however, the processes behind a lot of core legal work may actually be quite similar, and, therefore, ripe for disruption. Electronic discovery may be one of the most obvious examples of a legal process that went through this type of disruption. When the troves of electronically stored information became too big for review by traditional methods, e-discovery providers, many of whom have evolved into today’s ALSPs, were engaged to provide process, technology enablement, and flexible staffing models. At this point, many consider e-discovery and document review work to be fully commoditized. And from a legal perspective, it may look nothing like higher-level work that sits in the “core” (or, everyday) bucket. But many engineers look for process commonalities, and through that lens, a great deal of the core legal work law departments do every day may be ripe for process orientation, technology enablement and updated staffing models. From this perspective, more work fits into that “core” legal work bucket. Here are three alternatives to the traditional or hourly billing model for delivering legal services. When implemented strategically, they can drive much more than just cost savings. 1. Productization and Self-Service Deploying a combination of people, process and technology in new ways is driving much of the innovation in the legal marketplace. One way to describe their coalescence is “productization.” The concept of productizing legal services may be unknown or off-putting to many in the legal realm who may infer a more commercialized approach based on “products” that do not allow them to utilize their specific expertise. To many businesses, however, productization is simply the packaging of people, processes, and technology to solve a problem and deliver value at scale, and it is one of the most important components of success. In software companies, for example, a key ingredient to success is the ability to identify use cases that have become so commonly needed that a standard solution can be implemented at scale across many customers. A software company that fails to focus on productization and instead must build bespoke solutions for each customer may inevitably find it difficult to scale and grow. Similarly, this failure to find standards limits the amount of work that legal departments can deliver to their internal clients. One strategy that legal teams can employ is to focus on processes that are supported by no-code or low-code platforms that empower customers to create workflow automations on their own or in partnership with process experts (or “legal engineers”). In many ways, this is a win-win for legal teams. They can leverage tools with the flexibility to solve their unique challenges while still taking advantage of technology to support standard, best practice processes and workflows. These same tools can also enable a self-service model that empowers the consumers of legal services to do some things for themselves instead of relying on direct involvement from legal. 2. Disaggregation Under the traditional model, law departments typically send some work to their firms and keep some for themselves. But newer service delivery models can provide clients with more options—and more flexibility. Projects can more effectively be disaggregated and split among a variety of providers, separating the work that must be done by lawyers from work that can be done by other professionals. For example, rather than sending all M&A work to a large firm, a more sophisticated client might negotiate the final agreement in- house, sending the regulatory or antitrust work to a big firm and the due diligence to an ALSP. However, such a strategy typically requires a higher level of project management to ensure task clarity and that work is done by the right resource, in the proper sequence, and done to the appropriate standard relative to the risk involved. This will also require some rebalancing of the workforce in line with the strategy. 3. Alternative Legal Service Providers ALSPs are businesses that deliver work products under the direction of the legal function. Some are onshore, some are offshore, and some are even embedded inside a law firm or have teams embedded in corporate legal departments. ALSPs come in different varieties that include, standalone boutique organizations, and specific offerings from broad-based consulting organizations to integrated services. Over the past decade or so, new technologies and providers have disrupted the traditional service model, creating new options for the handling of core and commodity work. Taking the burden of more routine work away from in-house and law firm attorneys is not just a cost- reduction play. It allows them to focus on higher-value work like managing risk or overseeing important litigation. It also creates a career path for some attorneys and legal professionals who can specialize in other work under more robust project management protocols. Of course, one size does not fit all. An efficient way for law firms and legal departments to implement a strategy for managing legal work may be to create a sourcing framework which enables them to identify and design a hybrid approach to delivering legal services. While this may seem obvious, implementing such a strategy is not always simple. It typically requires the resources, openness, and desire across the legal department and its firms to not only design but also adopt new practices. With the right focus on change management, however, the application of new service delivery models can provide enormous value to a legal department and the larger enterprise. Robert Taylor Managing Director, Legal Business Services Deloitte Tax LLP Email: roberttaylor7@deloitte.com

"Stakeholder engagement strategies across the aluminum value chain in Brazil”
publications.publishedAt: Consilience: The Journal of Sustainable Development · Jan 1, 2010
publications.description: In 2008 Instituto Observatório Social (IOS) and Centro de Estudos das Negociações Internacionais (CAENI) embarked on a research and field project to study the labor situation as well as the environmental impact of five aluminum companies in the north of Brazil. While preliminary findings indicated that companies adhered to labor laws and regulations and invested in technological improvements in order to tackle environmental issues, there remained significant resource inequalities across stakeholders in the aluminum value chain. Nevertheless, both local government and civil society often remained acquiescent to the status quo established by companies. IOS and CAENI identified a need for further research on the impact of mining and corporate social responsibility (CSR) practices on local development and sustainability issues, as well as Brazil’s role in the global aluminum value chain. They invited a team of students from Columbia University’s School of International and Public Affairs (SIPA) to research the feasibility of a multi-stakeholder engagement or social dialogue, by studying and analyzing the aluminum value chain and performing a stakeholder mapping in the affected areas. IOS/CAENI can act as a monitor of a social dialogue across the aluminum value chain in Brazil, and as such, help stakeholders to identify opportunities to maximize positive externalities across the aluminum value chain, while ensuring sustainable development. IOS/CAENI will be essential in bridging the informational gap existing between local and global networks, taking full advantage of the international projection of the aluminum value chain. Finally, the team hopes the different stakeholders will use this report as a strategy for building stakeholder engagement into their own analysis.

publications.title: Eat glass and walk on fire, while managing a pandemic: Narratives of African American women who serve as senior housing officers
publications.publishedAt: Journal of Diversity in Higher Education · Jan 26, 2024
publications.description: Combatting racism and sexism is a daily occurrence in the professional and personal lives of African American women, including those working in higher education. The COVID-19 pandemic, which created uncertainty and stress and drastically changed how higher education operated, along with racial unrests following several highly publicized murders of Black individuals by police in the summer of 2020, and a highly contested presidential election in Fall 2020 created additional challenges. This narrative inquiry study explored the experiences of African American women who were serving as senior housing officers (i.e., directors of housing and/or residence life) at predominately White institutions during the first 18 months of the COVID-19 pandemic. Findings highlight how the intersections of racism and sexism shaped the experiences of our participants. Participants encountered barriers when striving to lead authentically while feeling pressure to succeed in managing pandemic-related challenges, not only for their department but their institutions. Participants also felt compelled to serve as voices for communities of color on their campuses while dealing with racism and sexism in their everyday professional lives. These experiences forced participants to re-evaluate how they were presenting at home and at work, and even led some to question their future in the field. As housing and residence life positions often serves as an important steppingstone in the pathways of senior student affairs officers, this study can provide valuable insights into the ways in which intersections of racism and sexism disrupt the pipeline to senior student affairs positions for African American women. publications.publishedAt: Deloitte Tax LLP and SAP US · Jun 25, 2020
publications.description:
The United States-Mexico-Canada Agreement (USMCA) is set to enter into force on 1 July 2020. Are your business’s global trade systems prepared and ready?  What changes need to be made to your SAP Global Trade Services (GTS) solution? What other operational changes should be considered?  

During this webcast, we’ll discuss:
•	Preparedness for the USMCA’s entry into force; 
•	Industries that will likely be the most affected; and
•	Reconfiguration or other changes required to SAP GTS technology to maintain compliance under the new USMCA requirements.

publications.title: Transitioning to USMCA: Key operational challenges and potential opportunities
publications.description:
As the COVID-19 pandemic continues to impact global trade operations, go-live of the United States, Mexico, Canada Agreement (USMCA) remains imminent. How are companies addressing the operational challenges that come with migrating to a replacement trade agreement midyear? What operational and automation opportunities does the USMCA present?

During this webcast, we’ll discuss:
- The latest update on the USMCA’s entry into force date
- How the USMCA is modernizing the North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA) qualification procedures and changing the rules of origin
- Industries that will likely be the most affected
- Operational considerations for implementation of the USMCA and a successful transition from NAFTA
- Reconfiguration or other changes required to Global Trade Management technology to maintain compliance under the new USMCA requirements

Dr. Osman serves as a technical lead and manager, leading data science teams to successful implementation of AI and ML systems within SFL's Energy, Resources & Industrials division, as well as the Life Sciences and Healthcare division. He possesses a robust foundation in natural language processing, computer vision, time series analysis, anomaly detection, and deep learning. Dr. Osman's expertise encompasses AI strategic development, solution design, implementation, and deployment.


Dr. Osman holds a wealth of experience in conceiving, creating, implementing, deploying and leading numerous AI projects for both commercial and government entities. Key projects encompass: automated visual inspections for jet engine parts utilizing robotics and computer vision, non-intrusive cyber-attack anomaly detection for electrical grids, strategic AI opportunities identification for a major aerospace contractor, optimization of load patterns and equilibrium cycles for a global nuclear energy entity, and automation of extraction, tagging, and generation for regulatory documents for a prominent pharmaceutical company.

This post is in strong support of Ahmad Osman as a neuro-engineer.  I am Ahmad Osman’s major PhD advisor for his degree plan in Biomedical Engineering (BME) at the University of Connecticut. I met Ahmad Osman in a graduate BME course I teach on “Neural Coding for Bionics”.  The class sparked an interest in Ahmad and he decided to pursue a Ph.D. degree in the area of neuro-engineering.  Ahmad is an excellent scholar.  Ahmad joined our PhD program with a M.S. and having published two papers with Pieribone at Yale University on developing a head-mountable optical imaging camera (2011, 2012).  I like to brag that Ahmad made the highest grade in the BME course called, “Neural Signal and Systems”, taught by my colleague Monty Escabi, as this is a notoriously difficult but important class for our neuro-engineers. Charmingly, Ahmad is very modest about this and other significant accomplishments. 
Ahmad’s Ph.D. thesis examined how neurons in three cortical brain areas encode timing cues in sound.  Specifically, Ahmad and colleagues discovered and modeled a novel power law relationship between spike train encoding time (and jitter) with sound timing cues that are important for perception of timbre and loudness in sound. This work is published in the Journal of Neurophysiology (2016).  Ahmad’s thesis also examined how spiking patterns from these neurons can be used to classify an array of different sound sequences (in preparations, 2017).  As part of this, Ahmad created a model “integrator” that integrated output form cortical neurons on different time scales and then he used optimization routines to find the optimal time scale for integrating and discriminating sequences of sounds.  In addition, Ahmad developed and cross-validated a probabilistic Bayesian model to determine how the timing of spikes could be used to code for the timing of change in sound envelope amplitude. These new discoveries and the rigorous computational models have already begun to make an impact in neuroscience and likely will impact a new generation artificial intelligence programs for sound identification.  
On a general level, Ahmad has proven to be a facile thinker and programmer that is able to readily take on complex ideas and adapt or write code to test his theories and predictions.  Moreover, Ahmad is excellent at public speaking having presented his work in several arenas including at MIT, Society for Neuroscience, and Neuroscience at Storrs.  Indeed, he won an award for presenting in the latter conference. Along these lines, Ahmad has been ranked highly as an instructor for the BME course on “Sensory Neuroscience” that involves teaching students rudimentary MATLAB and principles of acoustics and neuro-engineering.  In addition, Ahmad has been an inspiring leader of a team of students working with him on his thesis project.

publications.title: Neural spike-timing patterns vary with sound shape and periodicity in three auditory cortical fields
publications.description: Mammals perceive a wide range of temporal cues in natural sounds, and the auditory cortex is essential for their detection and discrimination. The rat primary (A1), ventral (VAF), and caudal suprarhinal (cSRAF) auditory cortical fields have separate thalamocortical pathways that may support unique temporal cue sensitivities. To explore this, we record responses of single neurons in the three fields to variations in envelope shape and modulation frequency of periodic noise sequences. Spike rate, relative synchrony, and first-spike latency metrics have previously been used to quantify neural sensitivities to temporal sound cues; however, such metrics do not measure absolute spike timing of sustained responses to sound shape. To address this, in this study we quantify two forms of spike-timing precision, jitter, and reliability. In all three fields, we find that jitter decreases logarithmically with increase in the basis spline (B-spline) cutoff frequency used to shape the sound envelope. In contrast, reliability decreases logarithmically with increase in sound envelope modulation frequency. In A1, jitter and reliability vary independently, whereas in ventral cortical fields, jitter and reliability covary. Jitter time scales increase (A1 < VAF < cSRAF) and modulation frequency upper cutoffs decrease (A1 > VAF > cSRAF) with ventral progression from A1. These results suggest a transition from independent encoding of shape and periodicity sound cues on short time scales in A1 to a joint encoding of these same cues on longer time scales in ventral nonprimary cortices.

publications.title: Continuous Time Level Crossing Sampling ADC for Bio-Potential Recording Systems
publications.publishedAt: IEEE Trans Circuits and Systems · Jun 1, 2013
publications.description: In this paper we present a fixed window level crossing sampling analog to digital convertor for bio-potential recording sensors. This is the first proposed and fully implemented fixed window level crossing ADC without local DACs and clocks. The circuit is designed to reduce data size, power, and silicon area in future wireless neurophysiological sensor systems. We built a testing system to measure bio-potential signals and used it to evaluate the performance of the circuit. The bio-potential amplifier offers a gain of 53 dB within a bandwidth of 200 Hz–20 kHz. The input-referred rms noise is 2.8 uV. In the asynchronous level crossing ADC, the minimum delta resolution is 4 mV. The input signal frequency of the ADC is up to 5 kHz. The system was fabricated using the AMI 0.5 um CMOS process. The chip size is 1.5 mm by 1.5 mm. The power consumption of the 4-channel system from a 3.3 V supply is 118.8 uW in the static state and 501.6 uW with a 240 kS/s sampling rate. The conversion efficiency is 1.6 nJ/conversion.

publications.title: Design Constraints for Mobile, High-Speed Fluorescence Brain Imaging in Awake Animals
publications.publishedAt: IEEE Trans Biomed Circuits Syst · Oct 1, 2012
publications.description: In this paper we present a fully self-contained imaging instrument (30 mm overall length) that is capable of recording high speed and detect relatively small fluorescent signals (0.1% ΔF/F) from brain tissues potentially containing genetically-encoded sensors or dyes. This device potentially enables the study of neuronal activity in awake and mobile animals during natural behaviors without the stress and suppression of anesthesia and restraint. The device is a fully self-contained illumination system, wide field fluorescence microscope ( ~ 4.8mm2 FOV-25 um lateral resolution-1.8 × magnification-0.39 NA) and CMOS image sensor (32 × 32). The total weight of the system is 10 g and is capable of imaging up to 900 fps. We present voltage dye RH1692 experiments using the system to study the somatosensory cortex of mice during whisker movements using an air puff.

publications.title: Head-Mountable High Speed Camera for Optical Neural Recording.
publications.description: We report a head-mountable CMOS camera for recording rapid neuronal activity in freely moving rodents using fluorescent activity reporters. This small, lightweight camera is capable of detecting small changes in light intensity (0.2% ΔI/I) at 500fps. The camera has a resolution of 32×32, sensitivity of 0.62V/lxs, conversion gain of 0.52μV/e(-) and well capacity of 2.1Me(-). The camera, containing intensity offset subtraction circuitry within the imaging chip, is part of a miniaturized epi-fluorescent microscope and represents a first generation, mobile scientific-grade, physiology imaging camera.

headline: Senior Life Sciences Consultant at Deloitte - Servant Leader | Optimist | Listener
about:
People are my passion. Working with individuals, teams, and organizations to brainstorm, innovate, drive and manage change energizes me, as well as empowering people - through onboarding, coaching, training, you name it. I aspire to inspire and my personal mission in life is to engage, educate, and empower those around me. 

As a Senior Consultant at Deloitte & Touche, LLP, I have served in the life sciences and healthcare industry for several years, helping clients improve business processes, manage projects, build and conduct risk assessments, execute audits, and develop compliance controls and documentation. In my free time, I enjoy serving non-profit organizations in volunteer leadership roles achieve their goals, solve problems and increase organizational effectiveness across the dimensions of people, process, strategy, structure, and culture. I recently served on the Board of Directors as the VP of Operations for a 501c7 and as Trustee of a 501c3 organization. 

I'm constantly seeking learning and growth opportunities. I graduated Summa Cum Laude with a Bachelor of Science (B.S.) focused in Health Systems Management and a Masters of Business Administration (MBA) focused in Management from Loyola University Chicago. Always striving to expand my skillset and leave a positive impact on my organizations and surrounding communities, I also earned a PhD in Organization Development and PMP certification. Now, I actively pursue training opportunities to increase my capacity and drive value. 

In my personal life, I've resided in Chicago and its suburbs my entire life but I enjoy traveling, studying new languages, and trying various cuisines. I have had the opportunity to work at a large healthcare system in Beijing and study abroad across various countries in Southeast Asia and it's these experiences, as well as being a first-generation student, that have formed my passion for celebrating diversity in the workplace and learning about and experiencing new cultures.

headline: Managing Director, Deloitte. Physician executive and Geriatrician committed to care delivery innovation, creating opportunity and advancing optimal health for individuals, families, & communities.
about:
I'm a primary care internist and geriatrician, public health professional, and commentator passionate about improving and redesigning care for underserved and vulnerable populations. I lead award winning teams.

Currently, I am a Managing Director at Deloitte and Executive Director of the Center for Health Solutions and Deloitte Health Institute 
 
From 2016-2020, I served as SVP and Chief Medical Officer of the American Hospital Association and President of HRET.  This included developing digital tools of patient safety in ambulatory environments, multi-sectoral collaborations, and age friendly health systems.

Until 2016, I was the first Chief Health Officer at the Illinois Health & Hospital Association. In this role, I spear-headed large improvement projects, including the Hospital Engagement Network (HEN), aimed at reducing readmissions and hospital-acquired conditions. I was instrumental in launching several improvement collaboratives; managed the Medical Executive Forum; led the Midwest Alliance for Patient Safety; launched a physician leadership academy, and designed and advanced a statewide high reliability initiative.

Prior to my work at Illinois Health & Hospital association, I was Managing Deputy Commissioner and Chief Innovation Officer for the Chicago Department of Public Health (CDPH). There, I led the implementation of Healthy Chicago, the city's public health agenda, and innovations in cross-sector partnerships, predictive analytics, epidemiology and informatics. Under my guidance, the department was recognized both nationally and internationally in their approach to using predictive analytics to improve food inspections, chronic disease, West-Nile and lead inspections. I led a groundbreaking initiative with Advocate South Asian Cardiovascular Center in developing the SAHEB (South Asian Healthy Eating Benefits Program). During my tenure, the Chicago Department of Public Health received an award from the National Forum for Heart Disease and Stroke Prevention.

I earned a B.A. from the University of Chicago; Doctor of Osteopathic Medicine (D.O.) from Philadelphia College of Osteopathic Medicine; Master of Public Health from the University of Illinois at Chicago; and Master of Public Administration from the Harvard Kennedy School of Government as a Zuckerman and Commonwealth Fund Minority Health Policy Fellow. I am board certified in Internal Medicine and Geriatrics.

Founded in 1944, the Health Research & Educational Trust (HRET) is the not-for-profit research and education affiliate of the American Hospital Association (AHA). HRET’s mission is to transform health care through research and education. HRET’s applied research seeks to create new knowledge, tools and assistance in improving the delivery of health care by providers and practitioners within the communities they serve.

Vision: The AHA vision is of a society of healthy communities, where all individuals reach their highest potential for health.

Mission: To advance the health of individuals and communities. The AHA leads, represents and serves hospitals, health systems and other related organizations that are accountable to the community and committed to health improvement.

AHA was located initially in Cleveland, where it was founded, and then in Washington, DC, from 1917 to 1920. In 1920, the association established its headquarters in Chicago, where the majority of employees are still located. The Washington office was established in 1942 in response to the pressures of shortages brought on by World War II. At that time, the Washington office served as an information center to assist members in contacting the proper federal agencies. Currently, it is the principal advocacy arm of the association. The Office of the President and AHA policy, communication, and national advocacy staff are located in the AHA Washington office.

publications.title: How Cities Are Using Analytics to Improve Public Health
publications.description:
By Bechara Choucair, Jay Bhatt and Raed Mansour

From clean water supplies to the polio vaccine, the most effective public health interventions are typically preventative policies that help stop a crisis before it starts. But predicting the next public health crisis has historically been a challenge, and even interventions like chlorinating water or distributing a vaccine are in many ways reactive. Thanks to predictive analytics, we are piloting new ways to predict public health challenges, so we can intervene and stop them before they ever begin.

headline: Senior Manager at Deloitte
about:
Senior Manager at Deloitte with 20 years of hands-on experience in user experience, design, and product strategy. Extensive background in collaborating with multidisciplinary teams on agile delivery of mobile and web applications, device interfaces, and end-to-end interactions for smart product ecosystems.
Led and contributed to projects across automotive, EV charging, telecommunication, financial services, connected home appliances, smart TVs, and complex digital platforms. Delivered services globally, with a primary focus on European markets.
Expertise centers on omnichannel experiences that seamlessly connect physical devices with digital touchpoints. Strong focus on uncovering real customer needs and expectations, translating insights into actionable strategies, and leading the full UX & UI design lifecycle—from research and design thinking to planning, execution, and governance.
Active contributor to the design community as an international design awards jury member, invited panel speaker, and project coordinator and jury member for TÜBİTAK incentive projects.

experience.position: Head of UX/UI Design • IoT & Automotive / R&D
experience.description:
Leadership of UX&UI Design team and UX related projects @ Vestel Electronics. 

• Had the privilege of leading a group of remarkable individuals who were passionate about their work, expertise, and their fellow team members. 
• Embarked on a mission to elevate UX and succeeded in raising the UX maturity level to an undeniable standard. Built a new culture accepted and integrated. 
• Close cooperation with the IoT software development groups (Mobile Applications, Cloud, AI&Big Data, Device Integration and Cyber Security) and IoT Product Management.

Most notable projects we've developed from scratch (understanding the user needs) to the end (final UX & UI documentation for delivery of the project to software groups):
o	"Evin Aklı / Sharp Home /Veezy smart home mobile application and TV ecosystem: Lets users monitor and manage Vestel's Wi-Fi connected appliances both from mobile app and TV app. 
o	 Electric vehicle charger device interfaces: Links AC/DC charger device interfaces with mobile apps and payment systems. 
o	“Drive Green Next”, “VEC” E-Mobility app: Allows control and preferences selection for Vestel electric vehicle charging stations. 
o	Automotive ecosystem projects: Includes cluster, infotainment screens, and related apps with an omnichannel interaction.
o	Amazon Alexa and Google Home: Integration of Alexa and Google Home screens and flows for Vestel TVs. 
o	VESTEL Huddle : Meeting/huddle room display interface serving a seamless meeting room experience to its users. 
o	Data dashboard: For anonymous data collected from Vestel TVs spread all over the world.
o	“Vfit+” app: Lets health and fitness monitoring through Vestel's wellbeing products.
o	“Ionia” app: Manages e-bike battery health, trip, and status information. 
o	“Vestel Smart Center” app: Controls all features on Vestel Smart TVs for an enhanced experience. 

These projects also globally recognized and honored with invaluable 60+ awards from world's most prestigious design competitions.

•	Proceeded with ongoing UX projects and initiated new ones.
•	Established company's UX team.
•	Initiated the company's UX journey as the sole UX designer, progressively expanding with the support of new designers.
•	Emphasized elevating UX awareness within the company, ensuring all technical groups embraced UX and UI development processes.

With the transformation of technology and its reflection in user experience field I voluntarily took the role of UX evangelist in my company.     

Smart TV 
First smart TVs globally released to the market around 2008s. Vestel also started development studies on smart TVs at that period. I worked on first portal project and smart TV user experience project (lead for outsource support).    

Ipod Dock TV
Designed for combining small screen sized TVs with media content and high quality sound. An Ipod dock is integrated to the foot to create the best solution in this technology transition period to turn the TV into a media/music/photo player with a quality sound. With the trend of designing the TVs with slimmer frames the space needed for a quality sound was disappeared. For solving this problem, I have developed two different small size TV designs that the sound system is located in the foot and support part where expected free space for sound is available. 

All-in-One PC
This started as a conceptual project and also be a part of my PHD thesis. 
•	3 different potential user groups for All-in-one PC are defined; 1. office users, 2. bank or travel agency users, 3. home users
•	User needs research made on real life users of each group (18+ people) at their own working environment
•	Customizable digital and physical design ideas developed for All-in-One PC customizable keyboard

Vestel Venus smart phones 
In the first period of 2010s, Vestel joined the dynamic and competitive smartphone business. For the Vestel Venus smart phone models we worked on the below UX and UI studies:
•	Venus Smart Phone Call Application (contributer)
•	Ve-cam Camera Application (contributer)
•	Smart Phone launcher themes design (outsource project management)

Electric Vehicle Charger (EVC)
With the transition of the company to novel areas like E-mobility and EVCs we started our work with "Drive Green" mobile app that works with Vestel EVC devices.

In this role, I experienced a significant global shift from CRT to LCD TVs between 2005 and 2007. Design and production companies swiftly abandoned CRT technology, adopting LCD and subsequently LED flat panel technology. Those able to navigate this rapid transition thrived, while others faded away. Fortunately, I had the opportunity to work as a designer during this transformative period at Vestel, a company that successfully navigated the European market. This transition presented new design and ergonomic challenges, and I was among the designers tasked with addressing these concerns.

•	Worked closely with product management and engineering development teams on global customers projects of TV family product design (CRT, LCD and LED), TV remote control design, settop box design and All-in-one PC design
•	CMF design of these products
•	Presentation of product design alternatives to Product Management groups, global customers and CEO level of top management
•	Created variations of physical mockups both low fidelity and high fidelity to review the ergonomics maturity
•	Ergonomics evaluation studies for remote controls considering the interaction with TV for defining button locations, groupings, relations and discoverability of icons
•	Usability studies for defining interaction flow between the remote control and TV menus

Commercial projects:

•	TFT LCD TV design (mass produced)
•	14” TV-DVD design (mass produced)
•	15”, 21”, 28”, 29”, 32” Real Flat TV family design (mass produced)

projects.title: Eliciting User Insights for New Generation TV Remote Controls - Vestel Electronics (Manisa, Turkey)
projects.description:
The design team of Vestel Electronics was working on the design of new generation TV remote controls. The team was interested to know the latent needs of middle-aged house wives associated with TV remote control usage. This user group was especially important for the company as the market research had shown that the television usage is the highest in this user group; however, they are not comfortable with technology. The company wanted to propose simple and meaningful solutions that this user group can also use with pleasure. 

In order to inform and inspire the design team of Vestel Electronics, during my master graduation project, I explored the usage of TV remote controls by middle-aged house wives. 

During this project my responsibilities include:

Design and execution of a contextmapping study with eight middle-aged housewives. 

Analysis of the results through Qualitative Thematic Analysis.

Distilling design insights from the data.

Design of an interactive database to share the results with the design team in an inspiring way.

featured.title: Writing = art; editing = science. You don't need to be drunk to do either!
featured.subtitle: Nidhi Vikram Choudhury on LinkedIn

slides.title: Writing = art; editing = science. You don't need to be drunk to do either!
slides.subtitle: Nidhi Vikram Choudhury on LinkedIn
slides.description: Ernst Hemingway did not say, "Write drunk, edit sober." That quote is often attributed incorrectly to him, did you know? And thank goodness someone clarified or else many an aspiring writer would have wasted away, searching for creativity at the bottom of the glass. Writing and editing: Two very different skills. Figuratively speaking, writing is an art, editing a science; writing is done from the heart and editing from the mind. These two are separate activities and must be, to the extent possible, completed by two different people. While a writer knows what will sell, and editor knows what reads well. Both are essential to a good piece of writing. I am sharing simple tips that I follow, while playing either role. While writing: Decide which of the five Ws will you cover (who, why, which, what, when), and how will you corroborate them. Examples, cases in point, numbers, or even quotes—whatever you can find, corroborate. Use your own idea and build upon it. A good writer is rarely influenced, only intrigued. The best books there are are filled with novelty. Develop a literary style. Whether it’s interrogatory, satirical, evolutionary, judgmental, or a simple opinion. Find a style and stick to it. Pour it all out and forget about what becomes of it. All the best written pieces have gone through written diarrhea. Writing is work and requires discipline. Keep at it every day. Definitely do not indulge in editing at this stage. While editing: Read the entire piece once completely. Add headings or titles to all the paragraphs to understand the structure and flow. Rearrange paragraphs as necessary for better flow. Ensure a sentence variety of simple, compound and complex sentences. Introduce the right transitions, but not too many. And then edit word by word. Most editors maintain checklists of common errors. Talk to the author; always. Most of us writers are our own editors. But if you do have the luxury of having the literary other present in your life, talk to each other. The best written pieces are teamwork built on mutual respect and admiration. What challenges do you face while writing or editing? Perhaps we can add to this list...

headline: CFO Advisory Manager at Deloitte UK
about:
Monica Allgaier, CPA, studied Accountancy, International Business, and Innovation, Design & Entrepreneurship at the University of Notre Dame Mendoza College of Business. Monica interned in Audit & Assurance at Deloitte US in Chicago and participated in Deloitte's International Internship Program working at Deloitte Australia in Sydney, Australia, in 2018. 

From 2019 to 2024, Monica spent over 5 years in Deloitte US's Audit & Assurance practice, including most recently in an Audit & Assurance Manager role in our Chicago, US office. 

From 2024 to date, Monica is a Manager - Accounting, Reporting & Advisory in Deloitte UK's CFO Advisory practice in our London, UK office, primarily focused on US Markets and Private Equity. 

Further, Monica is honored and humbled to serve on the NDDCEL (Notre Dame Deloitte Center for Ethical Leadership) and Notre Dame Mendoza Accounting Advisory Boards.

headline: Senior Manager, Behavioral Analytics & Data Science at Deloitte
about:
It has been my privilege to work with terrific folks in the areas of business development, intelligence, law enforcement, national defense, and public policy with a focus on machine learning/artificial intelligence applications to these areas.  Over my career I have moved up the statistical behavioral analyst chain from an analyst to project lead/Unit Chief/technical lead. I currently am a Senior Manager for Deloitte LLP,  supporting Deloitte LLP's growth in applying behavioral science-based machine learning and artificial intelligence to business analytics programs/projects.  

My goal is to continue to enable colleagues to do their best data science and social science research through generating new work for them, managing teams, mentoring, and creating a stable of satisfied clients/colleagues.  I look forward to engaging with clients and colleagues in order to develop studies that meet their needs and interests.  This goal is embedded within Deloitte LLP's larger goals of serving our customers and helping them solve their toughest problems.

Specialties: behavioral research, business analytics, contract management, criminal justice analysis,  counterterrorism analysis, foreign policy analysis, brand tracking, customer satisfaction surveys, data analysis, data collection, grant writing, government consulting, machine learning/AI, public policy analysis, presentations, public speaking, statistical programming, research design, report writing, R, SAS, SPSS, Stata, statistics, social science database administration, social science database design, social science database development, survey design, survey documentation, survey management, visual presentation of data

projects.title: Modeling Carbon Tax Policy Impacts on U.S. Commercial Airlines by using Agent-Based Modeling and Crowdsourced Data
projects.description:
The complexity of interactions between commercial airlines and the traveling public in the U.S. Air Transportation System (ATS) makes the evaluation of proposed ATS-related policy changes a challenging task. Proposed policies, such as a carbon tax, involve a continuous interplay of feedback and response between an airline’s operational and pricing decisions and customer purchasing decisions. A key component for modeling customerbased interaction outcomes is the ability to capture representative willingness-to-pay (WTP) perceptions of customers in the system. Insights for realistically parameterizing a modeling construct of customer WTP is especially challenging in the absence of relevant data, a common occurrence when the policy of interest is novel, untested, and/or has no implementation precedent in the context of the research question. To address this challenge, we present as a case study a notional industry-wide carbon tax that is implemented in an agent-based model of the ATS. To approximate the customer adaptive response—because no data exist within a U.S. implementation context—we use the online crowdsourcing platform Amazon Mechanical Turk to field a contingent valuation study that is then used to parametrize our model. The WTP curves of our customer agents are adjusted to represent the captured survey-based response to modeled airfare increases associated with implementation of the proposed carbon tax policy scenarios. Simulation results track with industry expert opinion on higher operational costs from a carbon tax being passed on to the customer through higher airfares, but despite the pricing increase, enplanements (ticket purchases) are generally maintained or increase over time given the adaptation of the traveling public to the pricing norm shift.

For the AIAA Aviation and Aeronautics Forum and Exposition, 2016.

projects.title: Improving LDA Topic Modeling with Gamma and Simmelian Filtration
projects.description:
Abstract— Twitter has become an important tool for communication and marketing. Topic model algorithms meant to characterize the discourse of online conversations and identify relevant audiences do not perform well for this task, despite their widespread usage. This paper proposes an iterative topic model, Gamma Filtration, and a social network based method, Simmelian Filtration, to amplify tweet-topic probability signal and reduce noise. We demonstrate the method on a novel data set collected of European Racially and Ethnically Motivated Violent Extremist (REMVE) networks on Twitter. We find that Simmelian Filtering is most successful at reducing noise as measured by perplexity. This improves our ability to detect and monitor core conversations of a community that is disseminating propaganda to increase online extremism.  
Keywords — Twitter, social media, topic modeling, latent dirichlet allocation, LDA, social network, violent extremism

projects.title: Dispelling the Myths: What Policymakers Need to Know About Pretrial Research
projects.associatedWith: Associated with Consulting to Pretrial Justice Institute
projects.description: The for-profit bail bonding industry has relied upon several recent studies to make the claim that commercial surety bonds are the most effective type of pretrial release. This paper provides an overview of those studies and explains why they cannot be used for this purpose because they do not answer questions about the effectiveness of any one type of pretrial release over that of others. This paper also cautions policy makers when the for-profit bail bonding industry presents them with these studies, and concludes that researchers should engage in objective and methodologically sound research that informs cost-effective and evidence-based pretrial public policy.
