experience.description: In this role, Mikala will rotate through four distinct specialties (including Mergers & Acquisitions, Valuation, Controllership, and Business Processes) each for six months for a total of two years.

Mikala was inducted into the Beta Sigma Chapter of Beta Alpha Psi (BAP) this April 2021. She assumed the role of Notre Dame chapter President for academic year 2021 to 2022. BAP is an international honor society for financial information students and professionals. Founded in 1919, it has over 300,000 initiated members from over 300 universities. BAP encourages the study and practice of accountancy, finance, business analytics or digital technology; provides opportunities for service, professional development, and interaction among members and financial professionals; and
fosters lifelong ethical, social, and public responsibilities.

Advancing further into her leadership career within the SIBC board, Mikala recently realized the role of Vice President. In contrast to her Chief Operating Officer position, in this role, Mikala offers a more directional and comprehensive leadership perspective; she helps to oversee the board of directors, guide the Council's annual objectives as well as assist the division directors with project fulfillment. Additionally, while working closely with the President, Mikala drives council-wide events and projects, conducts marketing efforts, and increases brand awareness across the Notre Dame community.

The Student International Business Council (SIBC) is an entirely student-run organization that offers undergraduate students at the University of Notre practical professional experience with companies  around the world. As the largest organization on campus, with over 2000 members, the council encourages students to develop leadership skills, cultivate their entrepreneurial ability, and hone in on both their soft and hard skill proficiency. The organization has 5 divisions, including Accounting, Consulting, Finance, Marketing, and STEM divisions, which each complete semester long projects or various other specialty ventures. SIBC also has 2 council initiatives of Social Impact and International Experience that influence some of the division projects.

Now as the Chief Operating Officer, Mikala plans the All-Council meeting each semester, liaises with ND Student Activities Office to conduct operations and oversee the email account on Gmail as well as the listserv on MailChimp. She also maintains the SIBC website, updating appropriately with accurate information each semester and assists the President and Vice President with special projects as necessary.

Previously in SIBC, Mikala was also a project leader in the Accounting Division for the Fall 2019 KPMG project. She led the rest of her group through a semester-long case project dealing with mergers and acquisitions, due diligence, and risk management.

Mikala was a travel team member for both the Spring 2019 Accounting Division BDO project, which delved into emerging technologies and the new tax reform, and the Fall 2018 Accounting Division EY project on revenue recognition. Her and the rest of the travel team members would meet and work weekly on a case provided by each firm listed above. Eventually, they created a final deliverable and presented their findings to the Chicago offices of each firm.

This Monday, I started my first week as an Accounting & Internal Controls intern at Deloitte, which is specifically housed under the Controls Compliance & Finance Operating Unit. My line of work delves into risk advisory: topics such as managing compliance complexity, improving confidence in strategic transactions, securely implementing tech and avoiding fraud, waste, and abuse. Although it is only the first week and I am still grasping the gist of the fast-paced profession, I am super excited to be working for Deloitte this summer and I cannot wait to continue learning in the upcoming weeks.

projects.title: Apoptosis in HeLa and Cos-7 cells as a consequence of transfection with TAP (NXF1) cDNA [Undergraduate Research Senior Thesis]
projects.description: ABSTRACT: The nuclear pore complex (NPC) mediates the exchange of materials between the nucleus and the cytoplasm. TAP, also known as NXF1, is a widely known receptor that helps export mRNA’s from the nucleus to the cytoplasm through the NPC. All eukaryotic cells produce a basal level of endogenous TAP to mediate mRNA transport. Although it is widely known that a majority of mRNA's use TAP for nuclear export, it is not known whether TAP is used for the export of pro-apoptotic mRNA. In unpublished observations, it was noted that cells transfected with exogenous TAP cDNA tend to increase in their expression of the TAP protein and then begin to die within 48 hours. This is an interesting observation because we expect to see an increase in protein expression after 48 hours post-transfection. Here, we wanted to study the link between transfection of TAP cDNA and the subsequent increase in cell death that occurs within 48 hours. We performed transfections in HeLa and Cos-7 cells using lipid transfection and electroporation methods, respectively. After transfection, cells were harvested at either the 24 or 48 hour time points and counted to determine the ratio of dead to live cells. The cell lysates were then analyzed using the western blot method to determine if an increase in TAP protein expression had occurred. We observed that no real change in TAP protein expression occurred in HeLa cells, but an increase in cell death at the 48 hour time point was noticed. In Cos-7 cells, we initially noticed a significant increase in cell death at the 48 hour time point, and a dramatic increase in TAP protein production.  However, in a replicated experiment, we noticed a decrease in TAP protein expression at the 48 hour time point in comparison to the 24 hour time point, and an increase in cell death. At this time, we are not fully convinced by these findings to conclude if an increase in TAP expression caused by transfection actually leads to apoptosis.

publications.title: Quality Engineering and Cloud: Real Lessons from the Field
publications.description:
Cloud technologies are helping organizations not only bring products and services to market at lightning-fast speed but also react to market trends quicker than ever before. And that has far-reaching implications on how quality is assured in the cloud.

Join Quality Engineering (QE) leaders for a fireside chat focused on how organizations can realize efficiencies in QE during cloud migrations.

We’ll explore:
• QE lessons learned from enterprise cloud migrations
• Nuances of tailoring QE to various cloud migration archetypes (the 6 R’s)
• Use cases of how AI-enabled next generation technologies are fostering innovations in testing tools and test data in the cloud
• Strategies to reposition existing QE workforce in the cloud

publications.title: Moving Quality to the Cloud
publications.description:
Moving Quality to the Cloud
In today's world, organizations are either born in the cloud or moving to the cloud. How they succeed will depend on their strategy and approach to operating in the cloud. One of the key elements for the success of such organizations, is testing and more so, Quality Engineering. We will discuss different Quality Engineering approaches or methodologies required by organizations that are adopting the cloud, whether migrating applications from on-premise to the cloud or maintaining a hybrid model or building it all in the cloud. This will cover various cloud deployment models, with inherent nuances, that require specific types of functional and non-functional testing to be performed, including the appropriate toolsets to enable automation. The key takeaway for the audience would be identifying the appropriate QE strategy for various deployment models and the toolsets required to be successful.

headline: Partner, National Global Trade Advisory Leader at Deloitte Australia
about:
David is the National Leader of the Global Trade Advisory Practice at Deloitte Australia. David has over 23 years Big 4 firm experience specialising in Customs & Global Trade. Prior to working in Melbourne David completed a 3 year secondment working in the Customs & Global Trade team in the United States based out of the Deloitte Chicago office. Prior to his secondment to the United States, David worked in the Customs & Global Trade team in the Deloitte and PwC Brisbane offices. David has extensive experience in assisting clients with:

- Customs Consulting from both a compliance and cost reduction perspective 
- Export Controls
- Excise Duty

David has worked for clients across a variety of industries including mining, manufacturing, retail, oil/gas, power, water, high tech, government and automotive. David’s primary focus has always been on developing strategies to minimise an importer’s customs duty liability. David has also worked extensively on customs valuation analyses, in particular customs valuation of related party transactions and the interplay and inherent conflict between customs valuation and transfer pricing.

David is a former Chair and current member of the Law Council of Australia Customs & International Transactions Committee and a member of the Australian Border Force's Compliance Advisory Group.

headline: SAP S/4 HANA, EWM & BRIM Technical Lead | 15+ Years in Global SAP Implementations, Data Migration & Integration | Driving Multi-Country Rollouts & Enterprise Transformations
about:
Accomplished SAP S/4 HANA and BRIM Technical Lead with 15 years of experience spearheading global enterprise transformations, data migration strategies, and large-scale SAP rollouts across 4 continents. Skilled at aligning technology with business goals, I’ve led multi-country implementations in USA, Europe, Asia, North Africa, and Latin America while ensuring system reliability, performance optimization, and seamless user adoption.
With deep expertise in SAP BRIM, EWM, RAP, CDS, AMDP, and ABAP developments, I specialize in technical solutioning, interface design (AIF, IDOC, Proxy, OData, RESTful APIs), and system integration across SD, FI, FICA, MM, PP, QM, Treasury, SAP PS and CS modules. I’ve successfully managed and mentored global technical teams of up to 10 consultants, driving on-time delivery of complex SAP programs while maintaining high client satisfaction.

Key achievements include:
- Leading multi-country rollouts for Fortune 500 clients, ensuring smooth cutovers and stable post go-live performance.
- Designing and executing data migration strategies with DMC and customized load templates in S/4 HANA 2021.
- Delivering performance-optimized solutions through AMDPs, CDS views, and ABAP enhancements.
- Driving cross-functional collaboration between global teams, stakeholders, and clients in challenging project lifecycles.

Certified as a SAP Citizen Developer Associate and trained in German language, I bring both technical depth and cross-cultural expertise to bridge business and IT. Passionate about leveraging SAP innovations to enhance enterprise efficiency, I thrive in complex, multi-national project landscapes.

publications.title: The Lasting Impact of a Criminal Record: Effects of Arrests and Incarcerations on Employment Status
publications.publishedAt: Schreyer Honors College | Pennsylvania State University · May 1, 2019
publications.description: The purpose of this study is to examine the “scarlet letter” of a criminal record in today’s society, specifically the lasting impact it has on employment. The current study aims to explain the impact of criminal justice contact, and how it can impact employment status. Given prior research largely uses audit studies with experimental design and focuses on individuals actively searching. The current study uses survey method analyses and targets individuals who are out of the labor force. This research is also unique because it focuses on young adults aged 20 to 24. Moreover, this research examines how race moderates employment status. By using the National Longitudinal Youth Survey 1997 (NLSY97), a nationally represented sample, this research found that both arrest and incarceration have a negative impact on employment status. The results also show prior incarceration is associated with a to a greater likelihood of an individual being out of the labor force, when compared to arrest. Additional results also show the relationship between criminal justice contact and being out of the labor force is the strongest among black respondents.

It would enable the user to select the party location, food caterer, sound planner, decorations planner and Liquor provider. headline: Consultant, Social Service Leader, Human Centered  Strategist
about:
With over 30 years of experience serving at-risk populations—including the homeless, medically vulnerable, disabled, and mentally ill—I have dedicated my career to driving impact in not-for-profit and public sector organizations. As an executive leader, I have partnered with governing bodies and overseen teams from 5 to 600, managing budgets ranging from $500K to $400M. My work with government agencies, especially within Health and Human Services (HHS), has centered on advancing innovative solutions and improving outcomes for vulnerable communities.

I am passionate about building high-performing teams and fostering organizational cultures that prioritize agility, human-centered design, and user research. Over the past 15 years, I have led multi-unionized workforces, implemented competitive bid processes for operational savings, and ensured fiscal responsibility through hands-on financial oversight—including managing performance-based government grants and complex, restricted funding. My fundraising accomplishments include securing major gifts, cultivating individual donors, and leading successful grant solicitations and special events. I am proud of my track record in coalition building, advocacy, and stakeholder engagement to drive policy and systems change.

Outside of work, I am committed to lifelong learning and community service, and I find inspiration in collaborating with others who share a vision for equity and inclusion. My approach is rooted in empathy, adaptability, and a relentless drive to create sustainable, positive change.

experience.description: Advised federal partners on best practices in child welfare performance management  and systems optimization.

The Senior Director of SAFEty (Securing Advancement, Freedom & Empowerment) Initiatives is responsible for approximately $40M, a staff of 400, and a team of seven direct reports including: the First Deputy Director, Managing Director of Program Operations, the Directors of Business Administration, Culinary Services, Finance, Operations, and the Assistant Director of Training.

The SAFEty programs include: Residential programming for unaccompanied children, which includes operation of nine distinct centers around the City of Chicago. Other programs include a group home setting that serves as a juvenile justice alternative to detention, Violence Recovery Services, and Freedom from Trafficking services. Of particular note is that the SAFEty unaccompanied children program prides itself on being one of the only programs in the country serving children from around the world. The program staff speak more than 30 different languages and deliver high quality, inclusive and culturally competent programming.

experience.description: Teen Living Programs is a 40 year old social service agency serving Chicago's homeless youth. The  Teen Living Programs builds community, hope and opportunity for youth who are homeless.  We address their immediate needs and help them achieve independence and stable housing.

StreetWise is a 20+ year-old workforce development agency focused on providing homeless adults with social service support and employment training so they can achieve personal and financial stability.

Achievements
• Achieved 122% budget growth over three ½ years, from $450K to $1M.

• Achieved a $275K cash reserve at close of FY14 from a FY10 operating deficit of $117K, in part by eliminating $60K in expenses within the first year without reducing personnel or service delivery.

• Grew development income from $167K in FY10 to $663K at the close of FY14 by tripling the number of individual donors, adding 15 new foundation grants and launching a series of special events including small fundraisers, directed mailings and a formal annual gala.

• Improved agency outreach and operations by forming multiple inter-agency collaborations, leveraging public/private partnerships, growing the volunteer base and expanding university internship programs.

• Increased client service delivery by 38%, from 450 clients at the start of FY11 to 623 at close of FY14.

• Conceived and implemented two new, successful social enterprises that allowed the agency to expand its mission while garnering wide media attention, significantly increasing awareness of the agency and, thereby, increasing donor giving.

• Improved the effectiveness of client services by implementing a comprehensive performance management system, hiring credentialed staff and developing team-based service delivery, resulting in 244 housing placements, 209 job training graduates and 182 financial literacy graduates.

experience.position: Managing Deputy Commissioner - Office of Homeless Services
experience.companyName: City of Chicago - Department of Family & Support Services (formerly Dpt of Human Services)
experience.description:
The Department of Family and Support Services is the City’s largest social service agency, providing programing and assistance to all ages, from children to the elderly, with a particular focus on issues of poverty and homelessness.

Achievements
● Managed operations and policy for the Homeless Services Division, staffed by a 40-person team responsible for $72M in annual awards and management of 177 homeless service and supportive housing contracts awarded to 90+ agencies.

● Managed operations and policy for the Emergency Services Division, staffed by a 120-person team with a $4.6M budget responsible for 24/7 homeless outreach, case management and emergency displacement services.

● Oversaw management of the City’s homeless shelter system, comprised of 4,000+ shelter beds across 170 agencies, to certify performance outcomes and quality assurance consistent with Federal, State and City regulations, including Chicago’s Plan to End Homelessness.

● Served as the City’s point person for emergency shelter needs, coordinating efforts with City departments, the American Red Cross and the Salvation Army. Major incidents included overseeing Chicago’s refugee relief programs for Hurricane Katrina (4,000+ served), the 2008 Chicago River flood (400+ evacuated) and the 2010 Haiti earthquake (200+ sheltered).

● Guided Mayoral policy and strategic planning related to poverty and homelessness, including opening the first City operated Veteran’s Affairs Office, developing and launching the Chicago Homeless Youth Task Force, and holding an executive leadership role in the development, implementation and evaluation of Chicago’s Plan to End Homelessness.

experience.position: Deputy Chief of Staff - Human Services
experience.companyName: City of Chicago - Department of Family & Support Services (formerly Dpt of Human Services)
experience.description:
The City of Chicago is the nation’s third largest municipality with a then annual budget of approximately $3B and a population exceeding 2.7M. As of 2012, 14.7% of the Chicago metropolitan area’s population, or more than 1.8 million, lived below the poverty line.

Responsibilities
● A member of the Mayor’s Cabinet, reporting directly to the Chief of Staff, with frequent interactions with the Mayor, Richard M. Daley, and Aldermen regarding poverty, jobs, and economic security.

● Operational liaison between the Office of the Mayor and the City’s eight social service departments, which collectively had budgets of almost $1B. Departments included: Aging, Chicago Housing Authority, Children & Youth Services, Human Relations, Human Services, Libraries, Office of Domestic Violence, and the Office for People with Disabilities. The position required policy and strategy management of each department to assure coordination of the Mayoral strategic plan.

● Social service sector team leader for implementation of the City’s first performance management system, which enhanced inter-departmental efficiency resulting in significant savings for, and greater public transparency of, departmental operations.

● Effectively led policy initiatives around the Mayoral Administration’s efforts to address poverty and homelessness by working with stakeholders, advocates, community groups and government officials to build consensus, bridge disagreement and achieve the Mayor’s strategic goals.

volunteering.description: Since 1980, the Chicago Coalition for the Homeless (CCH) has had a clear mission: “We organize and advocate to prevent and end homelessness, because we believe housing is a human right in a just society.”

Assisted the committee in developing recommendations to better meet basic human needs and improve health and social outcomes in the City of Chicago by the following: 
•	Strong Safety Net – Ensure the City has a plan to meet basic human needs – housing, hunger and health 
•	Bridge to Independence – Support the path to self-sufficiency to help people live independently and thrive through daycare, outreach to immigrant communities, job training, substance abuse treatment and re-entry services
•	Commitment to Public Service – Coordination and shared responsibility. Match the right partner with the right service – public, private or non-profit. Energize individuals and community organizations to take an active role in their communities and share responsibility for success  
Citizens of Chicago will experience positive change as a result of these recommendations in the following ways:
•	Chicagoans will have access to the basics – housing, food, and healthcare
•	Chicagoans will understand the public health and social priorities of the City and contribute to their success
•	Chicago will have a public health agenda/strategy the execution and impact of which our citizens will be able to observe
•	Chicago taxpayers will know where their money is going and the results it is buying

I have the honor of serving as Deloitte’s US AI & Engineering Leader. Our team of 35,000 professionals is all about engineering for business advantage! As a principal in Deloitte Consulting LLP, I have had the privilege of leading technology-focused teams and client projects across a variety of industries, with a special focus on financial services and government & public services. Outside of work, you can find me and my husband fly fishing (a new hobby we’ve picked up), trying out local Chicago restaurants, or visiting our two amazing children at college!

publications.description: This document contains Minimum Aviation System Performance Standards (MASPS) for Aeronautical Mobile Satellite (Route) Services (AMS(R)S) that provide safety communications to aircraft in airspace where 1) procedural separation is applied or 2) ATS surveillance services are provided. System-specific material as defined in Section 5 are provided as attachments to this document. Each system-specific attachment describes the system that provides AMS(R)S and will contain information detailing system compliance with the requirements in the main body of this document and verification plans. Previous revision included an attachment for Inmarsat Swift Broadband Specific Material. This revision includes the addition of an attachment containing requirements for Iridium Certus AMS(R)S equipment.

publications.title: RTCA DO-262F Minimum Operational Performance Standards for Avionics Supporting Next Generation Satellite Systems (NGSS)
publications.description: This document contains minimum operational performance standards (MOPS) for avionics that provide Aeronautical Mobile Satellite (R) Services (AMS(R)S) by means of satellite communications technologies scheduled to become operational in context of the global and regional ATM and CNS modernization (e.g. ICAO/Global Air Navigation Plan, Europe/SESAR, US/NextGen). Previous release included an appendix containing normative requirements for Inmarsat equipment. This revision includes the addition of an appendix which contained normative requirements for Iridium Certus AMS(R)S equipment. A companion document DO-343(), Minimum Aviation System Performance Standards (MASPS) for the Aeronautical Mobile-Satellite (R) Service (AMS(R)S) as Used in Aeronautical Data Links, should be consulted for operational requirements at the air/ground system level, and for details of specific systems providing AMS(R)S.

headline: Managing Director at Deloitte Touche Tohmatsu
about:
Brian is a seasoned security leader responsible for protecting a US$ 67 billion global organization with over 450,000 professionals serving clients in over 150 countries and territories.  

He is currently a Managing Director in Deloitte’s Global cybersecurity organization, reporting to the Global CISO and currently serving as the CISO for Deloitte’s global entity.  

He also leads Global Cybersecurity Strategic Programs.  In this role he is responsible for driving multiyear transformational programs to globalize cybersecurity as well as cybersecurity governance, global cybersecurity assessment services, cybersecurity culture and other initiatives.  

Brian joined the Deloitte U.S. Firms in 1999 and performed information security consulting services for many significant Deloitte clients.  In 2003 he joined the growing internal global security function to build an organization charged with securing Deloitte’s global applications. After assuming several expanded roles, he was promoted to Managing Director in 2011. 

He has led and managed a comprehensive global information security organization with teams responsible for the security of applications, infrastructure, operations, threat monitoring, intrusion detection and security relationship management across Deloitte’s global entities.  

Highlights of Brian’s contributions include leading the establishment of numerous cost-effective security projects including global Internet/intranet vulnerability identification, comprehensive static and dynamic application security testing, network/host based IDS implementation, ISO 27001 certification, PKI deployment, and country security maturity evaluation criteria.

Brian plays an active role in many leadership development programs; to develop and evaluate prospective leaders for promotion and guide their ongoing professional development.

Brian and his wife, Ashley, live in Chicago with their two daughters.

Chief Futurist, Deloitte Consumer Industry | Leading the Future of the Consumer Industry
As the Chief Futurist for Deloitte’s Consumer Industry practice, I lead the Future of the Consumer Industry program globally. My team and I partner with forward-thinking consumer organizations to empower them in making bold decisions, helping them to become valued brands of tomorrow.

Driving Innovation and Transformation
In my 28-year tenure, I have:
•	Helped launch Deloitte Digital, Deloitte’s Digital Agency
•	Led the development of Deloitte's Omni-Channel & Digital Retail Market Offering.
•	Spearheaded the firm's predictive analytics go-to-market approach in the consumer industry.
•	Envisioned and helped establish ConvergeCONSUMER, driving innovation in customer experiences and operational decision-making through predictive analytics and key technologies. 

Global Impact and Thought Leadership
I have been instrumental in many of industry's largest consumer transformation initiatives, helping the world's leading consumer companies evolve into next-gen business models. My work spans innovative customer experiences, transformative business models, profitability and cost management, heart-of-the-business operations, and cutting-edge technologies.

I focus on large-scale transformation efforts that involve setting strategy and scaling a company's people, processes, and systems. My research and insights are frequently quoted in major media outlets, including The Wall Street Journal, Financial Times, ABC News, Reuters, CNBC, Internet Retailer, Multi-Channel Merchant, Chain Store Age, and Investor’s Business Daily.
Key Accomplishments and Speaking Engagements

publications.title: Becoming the Predictive Enterprise
publications.description: The consumer industry faces a transformative time, driven by shifting demographics, accelerating technology, collapsing barriers to entry, and evolving consumer behaviors. To thrive in this environment, integrating external data and predictive AI can help organizations uncover forward-looking signals—allowing them to better anticipate consumer needs and dynamically respond to market conditions.

publications.title: Mass to Micro: Meeting Unprecedented Market Shifts
publications.description: The consumer industry was built on economies of scale, mass production, mass distribution, and mass marketing. And this approach worked post WWII, while the market was growing, consumer spending was growing and product availability and distribution dictated markets. But as consumers become more nuanced—and their preferences more specific, and barriers to entry fall, future success in the industry will likely require different strategies.   The market is moving from Mass to Micro, yet most companies were not built to operate in this competitive environment.

publications.title: The Rise of Digital Goods and Services
publications.description: Digital offerings are evolving at a lightning pace. From health and fitness apps that personalize to their users, to smart collars that digitally monitor our pets, the convergence of cloud, Internet of Things (IoT), artificial intelligence (AI), and other technologies are helping an explosion of new digital goods and services permeate more corners of everyday life. Gen AI is poised to super-charge the shift of consumer spending from traditional categories to digital goods and services.    Is this a threat or opportunity for your organization?

publications.title: Buying Into Better: The Future of the Consumer Industry
publications.description: The consumer industry is on the precipice of dramatic change that over the next decade will impact the markets, models, and mechanics of consumer industry companies in significant ways. With all this uncertainty, one thing is clear: The strategies that led you to where you are now likely won’t get you to where you need to go next.

publications.title: The 6 Forces Shaping the Future of the Consumer Industry
publications.description: Through extensive research, Deloitte leaders have identified six key forces that will play a pivotal role in shaping the consumer industry, the business landscape, and the world over the next decade. In this time of unparalleled market uncertainty, consumer industry executives have the power to lead the charge of buying into better.

publications.title: The future is coming ... but still one day at a time: Seven data-driven trends defining the future of the retail and consumer products industry
publications.description: The retail and consumer products industry is hungry to predict the future, yet most predictions are prophetic, not practical. We took a different approach—looking deeply into the data and macro forces to highlight seven trends that are fueling the industry in the United States.

publications.title: The consumer is changing, but perhaps not how you think
publications.description: Contrary to conventional wisdom, there’s been no fundamental rewiring of the consumer. The modern consumer is a construct of growing economic pressure and increasing competitive options.

publications.title: The Great Retail Bifurcation
publications.description: Is the retail industry—especially the traditional store—on the verge of apocalypse? An in-depth survey tells a more nuanced story, one based on a stark income bifurcation and its impact on a changing industry.

publications.title: The Jason and Scot Show - Guest Appearance - Kasey Lobaugh
publications.description: Kasey Lobaugh joined the Jason and Scott show to talk about retail, disruption and retail strategy.

publications.title: The New Digital Divide: The Future of Digital Influence In Retail
publications.description: In the fourth installment of the Digital Divide, Deloitte continues to establish that retailers undervalue and under-deliver on the topic of digital.    While, today, retailers almost universally recognize that digital has reshaped customer behavior and shopping forever, many traditional brick-and-mortar retailers are still far behind at creating the digital experiences that customers really want.

publications.title: The Deloitte Retail Volatility Index
publications.description: Since 2010, volatility in the retail industry has increased 250 percent, resulting in $200 billion more of retail sales being “traded” among competitors. Our latest study measures disruption in the industry through results of the Deloitte Retail Volatility Index (RVI). This index quantifies the volatility and fragmentation in the US retail market, revealing that small and mid-level players are collectively stealing share from big retailers. Explore retail market share distribution changes in the top 100 retailers, how you can use RVI to predict the future of the industry, and ways to create a strategy for staying afloat during these tumultuous times.

publications.title: Retail Talent Disrupted
publications.description: Spurred by the digital revolution and the demands of an evolving consumer, new companies have entered the marketplace with innovative business models that threaten to make traditional retailers obsolete. Emerging retailers with “digital” in their DNA are challenging the ways many traditional companies acquire customers, compete in the marketplace, and configure their business.

publications.title: Navigating the Digital Divide: Global Edition
publications.description: The Global edition of this report explores the digital preferences of consumers, especially how the use of digital devices impacts in-store shopping behavior. It is based on a survey of thousands of consumers in nine different worldwide markets.

publications.title: What Got You Here Won't Get You There: Evolving the Merchandising Function in Today's Battle for Share
publications.description:
Technology has rewritten what consumers demand, what retailers are capable of, and how retailers compete with one another.  Assortment as a concept is no longer tightly bound to physical
inventory. A customer relationship can be just as strong over a thousand miles as it used to be over a few city blocks.  This piece evaluates the changing role of Merchandising in today's battle for market share.

publications.title: The retail transformation: Cultivating choice, experience, and trust
publications.description: New technologies and new ways to connect with consumers are transforming the retail sector. To compete effectively, traditional retailers should reimagine how they create and capture value, thinking past omnichannel positioning to find the best uses for their assets.

publications.title: Navigating the New Digital Divide
publications.description: For the third year, Deloitte Digital conducted surveys with thousands of consumers to understand how they engage with digital when shopping, and to quantify how these interactions influence their in-store purchase behavior. This year, and over two million data points later, the continuing growth of digital influence is resulting in a widening divide between consumers’ digital expectations and retailers’ ability to deliver on them.

publications.title: New Leaders for Retail Differentiation
publications.description: Three new CXO positions are becoming part of various retailers' change management process. But which is right for a particular retailer? Are they mutually exclusive? Does the organization need them all? Or are they all a leadership fad?​

publications.title: The New Digital Divide
publications.description:
Digital devices’ influence on in-store purchase behavior is growing much faster than anyone could have anticipated. Deloitte’s research shows that today digital technologies influence 36 percent or $1.1 trillion of in-store retail sales, and this number will likely increase to 50 percent of in-store sales by the end of 2014.

Given this acceleration, we are at a tipping point in retail — a point where digital channels should no longer be considered a separate or distinct business. Instead, digital is fundamental to the entire business and the entire shopping experience, in and out of the store. As this new reality begins to have a greater impact, retailers should change dramatically the way they think, measure, and invest in digital, and address their customers’ digital needs and wants.

publications.title: The Mobile Influence Factor
Deloitte's 4th Annual eCommerce Assessment
publications.description:
Our 4th annual assessment suggests that online capabilities can be categorized into three key themes. Each highlights a competitive building block that online retailers should consider when competing in the eCommerce market. They include:

* Critical Mass. Mature capabilities in the landscape that are critical to eCommerce success.
* On the Verge. Developing capabilities that online retailers have an opportunity to improve.
* The Next Wave. Visionary capabilities that are leading the market.

He worked directly with senior Sales and Marketing business leaders within the client organization. Despite the challenges of working remotely at the start of the pandemic, Greg built trust and strong relationships with stakeholders he had no prior relationship with. These relationships were crucial for us to deliver what became the most successful implementation at the organization.

His direct team members and immediate client stakeholders were distributed globally. Greg was able to bridge the communication challenges and information gaps between team members and across teams by fostering a collaborative atmosphere at all times.

Greg’s most impressive quality was his ability to set an example for his peers and his direct reports by bringing empathy to the table, for a team impacted on a personal front by COVID. As a leader, empathy in leaders on my team is one of the most important qualities. And it is a quality that is natural to Greg.
